text:
jess_cs: Heads up — ACME reports repeated 503s and timeouts since 12:03 UTC. They say errors started right after we pushed the quantized vicuna-13b swap. Customer-facing pages show latency spikes and 500/503s, several request IDs attached.

owen_oncall: on it. Can someone pull the runner logs for that window? any correlating autoscaler events?

kai_sre: I see a cluster of container restarts on worker-pool-14 around 12:03-12:06 UTC. NVML reports OOM on GPU0 for pid 8421 then an abort.

maria_runtime: copying relevant log snippet:
```
[2025-11-09T12:03:15Z] infer-runner[8421]: cuda runtime error: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
[2025-11-09T12:03:15Z] infer-runner[8421]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8a1234
[2025-11-09T12:03:15Z] kernel: coredump written to /var/crash/infer-runner-8421.core
[2025-11-09T12:03:16Z] containerd: killing container infer-runner: exited with status 137
```

tom_eng: interesting — status 137 from containerd typically indicates OOM killed by kernel (or cgroup). Are we seeing memory leak after quant swap?

kai_sre: memory usage before crash: GPU0 resident set ~46GB, peak 48.2GB. Model footprint expected ~44GB quantized but KV prefetch and batchmap pushed it up. Prefetch concurrency was 8 at the time.

jess_cs: ACME provided two failing request IDs: req_20251109_120315_az and req_20251109_120318_bf. They said retries didn't help; customer is asking for root cause and ETA.

owen_oncall: Can we repro on staging with same model and prefetch config? If it's prefetch concurrency related, reducing concurrency or disabling prefetch should mitigate quickly.

maria_runtime: I started a repro on staging with vicuna-13b-quant + prefetch=8 and batch_size=4. After ~20s of steady QPS, container OOMs with same SIGSEGV. Attaching small command run we used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://staging-infer/api/v1/generate -d '{"model": "vicuna-13b-quant", "prompt": "x"}' --parallel 50
```

kai_sre: confirms: regression introduced in quant swapping path. The runtime's prefetch path doesn't account for changed KV size after quantization. We need patch to cap prefetch or recalc KV allocation.

support_bot: Incident alert created: #INC-2025-1109-03. Pager duty notified. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-1109-03

tom_eng: quick mitigation: 1) rollback model swap for hosted pool serving ACME (we can pin to previous fp16 variant), 2) reduce prefetch concurrency to 2 via route override, 3) enable fallback routing to lower-tier nodes. I can push the rollback now if we agree.

kai_sre: +1 to rollback. Also adding a temporary OOMGuard limiter to runtime that rejects prefetch when predicted allocation > 47GB. We'll push a hotfix to staging then prod if green.

jess_cs: ACME wants an ETA for fix and asks whether they will be billed for errors during outage. billing_ops, can you advise?

billing_ops: We'll credit error-rate impacted requests for the affected hour once SRE confirms incident window. Please send list of request IDs and time range. We'll treat as customer-impact credit, no further action needed for now.

nowen_oncall: (action list) 1) tom_eng rollback swap for worker-pool-14 to vicuna-13b-fp16 immediate. 2) kai_sre push OOMGuard limit in runtime config. 3) maria_runtime run canary with prefetch=2 and monitor for 10m. 4) jess_cs communicate ETA to customer: 30-45m for rollback + verification.

maria_runtime: rollback in progress to previous model for pool-14. Scaling down prefetch concurrently. I'll post canary logs in 5m.

jess_cs: messaging to ACME: "We observed an increase in GPU memory pressure after the quantized model swap causing container OOMs and worker restarts; we're rolling back the swap and throttling prefetch while we deploy a runtime limit. ETA ~30-45m. We'll credit affected requests." ok to send?

tom_eng: message OK. Also include that we have a fix branch: runtime#oom-prefetch-cap (PR open).

kai_sre: canary passed: no OOMs for 12m with prefetch=2, CPU/GPU stable. No SIGSEGV. Rolling the config to prod pool-14 now.

support_bot: Update: Incident #INC-2025-1109-03 status -> mitigated. All affected routes rolled back at 12:47 UTC.

jess_cs: ACME notified and appreciative of credit. Marking this thread for postmortem. Owner: kai_sre.

kai_sre: will lead postmortem. Preliminary notes: root cause = incorrect KV allocation logic after quant swap + aggressive prefetch concurrency; remediation = rollback + runtime OOMGuard + unit test coverage for quantized KV size calc.

jess_cs: thanks team. I'll close after postmortem doc is ready. :thumbsup:
